description: We are a creative crew of engineers, writers, and visual designers who believe that data without a narrative is just noise. We are building a interactive storytelling website of ROBOTS in space in their perspective.
summary: We developed The Last Footprint, an interactive detective-style website of NASA’s Opportunity (MER-B) Mars rover, paired a review paper written by me on Anti dust glass of solar cell so that no rover in the future will fail to communicate just because it dont have sufficient energy. Through scroll-driven storytelling, a 3D mission pass, a 2.2× forensic evidence lens backed by nasa data sets, and a 2018 global dust-storm opacity simulator, visitors examine Opportunity’s 5,111-sol journey across Meridiani Planum and uncover how atmospheric dust opacity and surface dust accumulation ended its mission.
details:
What It DoesThe Last Footprint is a space-detective website about Opportunity, a brave little robot rover that explored Mars for almost 15 years. Visitors get a 3D space pass, a giant magnifying glass, and a dust-storm slider to see how a huge red dust storm blocked the sun, drained Opportunity’s battery, and made it fall asleep forever.

How It Helps I have tried to make it friendly so it will be easy for little space enthusiasts to understand and written a review paper to help So no future Mars robot ever runs out of power.It is a special clear shield for solar panels with two smart tricks: a super-slippery coating (MTMS and silica) so sticky dust cannot hold on, and a gentle electric wave (EDS) that pushes dust right off without wipers.

Why It Matters & Why It Is Fun Instead of a boring science book, this project turns real NASA space clues into an exciting detective game. Clean solar panels mean future Mars rovers, landers, and astronaut homes will always have enough sunshine to stay awake and talk to Earth.

Tools & NASA Clues Used We built the website using HTML, Tailwind CSS, JavaScript, and Canvas on Google Sites, powered by real NASA rover photos, Mars maps, dust-storm records, and fake Mars dirt benchmarks.
